newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady to up in two-tiered market.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady to up in two-tiered market.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended steady to slightly higher in what traders described as a two-tiered market, firmer swaps that have been balanced by ample local supplies and lacklustre end-user demand.
Still, a bid for pipeline spec material was heard at $228 cif, up about $2-$4 from Tuesday, traders said.
The trader who made the bid was believed to be trying to push prices higher and capitalise on it with a large cargo loading out of Skikda and sold to Petrobras, sources said
The cargo was expected to load on Wednesday but some traders thought it may not have been loaded yet.
Feb swaps ended unchanged at $228/$229 cif, recovering about a $1 after crude oil rebounded this afternoon. March swaps also were steady at $220/$221.
"The current balance in the physical market isn't reflected in the paper or the swaps," said one trader. "The physical market is balanced. It isn't tight."
Offers were heard at $232 early on and then at $229.50 in the paper market for Dow spec material.
One end-user said he was also trying to sell an 8,5000 tonne parcel of open-spec material at $226 basis Rotterdam, but had found no buyers.
